intended_object: Given a morphism of sheaves f : F ⟶ G, the induced map of cochain complexes Γ(X, I•(F)) → Γ(X, I•(G)). Here I• is the library's functorial (Godement-type) flasque resolution and Γ(X, –) takes sections on the whole space. This reading comes from the docstring and from the file's naturality lemmas.
explanation:
The body applies the global-sections functor on ⊤, extended to cochain complexes (`mapHomologicalComplex`), to the morphism of resolutions `flasqueResolutionNat.asFunctor.map f`. In other words, it is the map on morphisms of the composite functor "functorial flasque resolution, then global sections". That matches the docstring. The abbrev is a shorthand naming the morphism component of that functor. Its only uses in the file are to state the naturality lemmas `flasqueAcyclicResolutionExtZeroComplexIsoSections_hom_naturality` and `flasqueAcyclicResolutionExtZeroHomologyIsoSectionsHomology_hom_naturality`, so it is internal plumbing rather than a notion with its own definition in the literature.

One caveat: the section variables `[CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [PrespectralSpace X]`, `HasSheafify` and `HasExt` play no role in the construction. Because they depend only on `X`, Lean may still add them to the definition's signature, and if so they narrow it needlessly. Since this is a technical device, I don't treat that as a faithfulness issue. Mathlib has no declaration for this specific map.
